I put the receipt email behind a new flag, `NOTIFIER_FF_RECEIPT_V2`, but there's no new receipt email in the repo yet, so turning the flag on right now would break receipts.

**Change:** in `services/notifier/notifier/email.py`, `send_receipt` uses the `receipt_v2` template when `NOTIFIER_FF_RECEIPT_V2=1`. Otherwise it keeps using the current `receipt` template. The flag is an environment variable because the notifier is deployed on its own and can't read the root `flags.toml`; that's the project's convention for this service. It's checked on every send, and any value other than exactly `"1"` counts as off.

I added tests for flag on, flag unset, and values like `"true"` or `"0"`. All 6 tests pass. I also listed the flag in the notifier README.

**Before you turn it on:**
- **No new template exists yet.** I couldn't find a new receipt template or code anywhere in the repo; there isn't even a `templates/` directory. `receipt_v2` is a name I picked for it. Whoever builds it needs to add `templates/receipt_v2.mjml` and a plain-text `receipt_v2.txt` with the same variables (`invoice_id`, `total_minor`). If the new email is meant to change more than the template, such as the subject or extra data, tell me and I'll move that behind the flag too.
- **The flag isn't gradual on its own.** An environment variable is all-or-nothing for each deployment, so a slow rollout means turning it on one environment or deployment at a time. If you want a percentage of customers, I can add bucketing by a hash of the invoice or customer id, with something like `NOTIFIER_FF_RECEIPT_V2_PERCENT`.

Nothing is committed yet.
